01200001.408270 FILMING PERMITS Fees for commercial filming and still photography in City facilities or in City right 
of way, not including City beaches or parks (includes fees for filming in public 
right of way and application fees). This activity was previously managed by the 
Public Works Department, but oversight is being transferred to the City 
Manager's Office in FY 2025-26.

HOSTING SVC
Revenues received from Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District (SMMUSD) 
to archive and host School Board meetings on the City's website. This service 
was previously managed by the Information Services Department, but oversight 
was transferred to the City Manager's Office in FY 2023-24.

01200001.408790 VIDEO PRODUCTION 
SERVICE

District (SMMUSD) and other partner organizations for video production 
services. Since the pandemic, the School District has been covering its own 
meetings, and CityTV staff services are no longer needed.

annual guarantee), which became effective on January 1, 2025.

01800004.401020 TRANSACTION AND 
USE TAX
Revenue from Santa Monica voter approved Measure Y, which added a one-
half percent Transaction and Use Tax to the previous sales tax rate beginning 
April 1, 2011 and Measure GSH, which replaced Measure Y and added another 
one-half percent to the tax effective April 1, 2017. Half of the Measure GSH 
Transaction and Use Tax revenues are paid to the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified 
School District for use of certain school district facilities. Additionally, 25% of the 
Measure GSH revenues have historically been set aside to be used for 
affordable housing. The affordable housing allocation was suspended for FY 
2020-21 and FY 2021-22 to help offset pandemic-induced revenue losses. 
Revenues should follow a similar pattern as sales taxes.

01800004.402000 TRANSIENT 
OCCUPANCY TAX
After being significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, Transient 
Occupancy Taxes (TOT), a tax levied by the City on transient room rentals, 
have recovered to pre-COVID levels. Measure CS, passed by Santa Monica 
voters in November 2022, effective March 1, 2023, increased the City's TOT rate

projected to increase reflecting a modest increase in average room rates and 
occupancy as well as major events coming to the region, including the 2026 FIFA 
World Cup and 2027 Superbowl.

57500001.409870. FUEL FLOWAGE FEE Fees are based on a percentage of fuel delivered at the Fuel Farm and Fuel 
Service Station located at the Airport. Fees are paid by the Fuel Service Station 
and the independent contractor that manages the Self-Serve Fuel Station, 
based on a percentage of the total gallons of Jet A Fuel and  Aviation Fuel 
(AVGAS). It is industry standard practice to use such fee revenues for the 
maintenance of the entire airport. The fee rate is established from time to time 
based on neighboring airport rates and is authorized by City resolution. Fuel 
Flowage Fee revenues are anticipated to remain flat for FY 2025-26 and FY 
2026-27.

60600002.401500 STA SALES TAX -

Sales Taxes                   3,197,272                   4,214,750                   5,819,886                 5,866,445                      5,925,110 
60600002.401510 TDA SALES TAX-
OPERATIONS
Transportation Development Act (TDA) revenues are funded by a 1/4 cent of 
the of the 7.25 cent statewide retail sales tax and deposited into a Local 
Transportation Fund (LTF) held by Los Angeles County. Funds are apportioned 
by the State Board of Equalization according to the amount of tax collections in 
each county. After deducting for administrative costs, the balance is distributed 
by Metro based on Metro's Formula Allocation Procedure (FAP) applied to the 
City's transit performance data. FY 2025-27 revenues are based on initial 
estimates of the funding marks and will be updated to reflect the final funding 
marks from Metro. FY 2025-27 revenue estimates have not been published, but

16500001.405680 MEASURE W ANNUAL 
REVENUE
In 2018, LA County voters passed Measure W (Safe Clean Water Program). 
Measure W generates funds for watershed projects, which are distributed in 
two ways: (1) the annual municipal transfer; (2) regional, one-time, grants 
awarded through a competitive process. This line item represents the annual 
municipal transfer. FY 2025-27 budget is based on a three-year average. This is 
a countywide assessment based on square footage of impervious area on a 
parcel. As private parcels are redeveloped, property owners may qualify for an 
exemption from this assessment; therefore, the total amount collected by the 
County will vary year over year, and not necessarily increase each year.

City Attorney
20120001.406021 STEP COURT-LAHSA There are nearly 1,000 people experiencing homelessness in the City of Santa 
Monica. Many of these individuals have mental health and/or substance abuse 
issues. As a result of their lack of stable housing and the addiction and mental 
health issues they face, many unhoused individuals are involved in the criminal 
justice system. To address this need, the City Attorney's Office created the 
Shelter, Treatment, and Empowerment program, otherwise known as STEP 
Court. A key component of STEP Court will be connecting low-level criminal 
defendants with a resource navigator to assist them in accessing necessary 
treatment and resources and to ultimately obtain permanent housing. The City 
is partnering with Exodus Recovery, Inc. to provide resource navigator services. 
Through this program and partnership, the parties hope to continue to reduce 
the number of unhoused individuals in Santa Monica. This is a local one-time 
grant, and funds will not be affected.
Intergovernmental                                      -                                      -                        50,000                                      -                                      - 
20120001.406120 SAMO BRIDGE GRANT The Santa Monica City Attorney’s Office in partnership with SMPD and Housing 
and Human Services have been awarded almost $8 million in Proposition 47 
grant funding from the State of California to create SaMo Bridge, a diversion 
program designed to address the behavioral health, substance abuse issues, 
and housing needs of justice involved adults in the Santa Monica community. 
SaMo Bridge will provide people who are stuck at the intersection of criminal 
justice involvement, addiction, unmet behavioral health needs and 
homelessness, a bridge into services to reduce recidivism. A key component of 
the program is a no-barrier 24/7 respite hub where the Santa Monica Police 
Department can divert people at the pre-arrest, post-arrest and pre-filing 
stages of law enforcement contact. At the respite hub, people can address 
basic needs and enroll in 90-day care coordination plans focused on securing 
housing and treatment services. Upon program graduation, the City Attorney 
will dismiss citations and cases. This is one-time grant funding from the State, 
reimbursing monthly and should not be affected.
Intergovernmental                                      -                                      -                   3,301,850                 4,624,322                                      -

20600003.420210 SM BLVD SAFETY ENH 
STUDY
The Santa Monica Blvd Safety Study will focus on analyze crash patterns on 
Santa Monica Boulevard, from Ocean Ave to the eastern city border, as well as 
observations and experiences shared by community members through a 
robust community engagement process. The project aims to improve safety for 
people walking, driving, and taking transit, and connect to major destinations 
and job centers. This study will result in a adopted plan to identify targeted 
safety enhancements and recommend preferred short-term and long-term 
improvements to the corridor.

21180001.525260 OTHER COSTS Asset seizure funds come from the Federal Asset Forfeiture Program, a nationwide law 
initiative that removes the tools of crime from criminal organizations, deprives wrongdoers of 
the proceeds of their crimes, recovers property that may be used to compensate victims, 
and deters crime. Federal law authorizes the Attorney General to share federally forfeited 
property with participating State and local law enforcement agencies, including the Santa 
Monica Police Department. Asset seizure funds are not budgeted in revenue nor expense 
since the amount received is unpredictable.
